lead: This week's digest lists 10 publications across Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics & Statistics, Neuroscience and Physics. The one cross-unit collaboration is a breast cancer drug delivery study involving Bruce McKay (Biology) with David Sabatino and Maria DeRosa (Chemistry). Biology also has an insect decline review and a bacterial genetics study, and Chemistry has a catalyst paper on converting CO2 to methanol. Computer Science has three papers (data leaks, display clutter, 3D shape generation), and Physics has an ATLAS supersymmetry search and a gallium nitride study.

items.title: Uncovering the importance of lipofection for aptamer-mediated therapeutic oligonucleotide delivery in a HER2+ SKBR3 breast cancer cell line
items.summary: The team modified a DNA aptamer that targets the HER2 protein so it carried antisense or siRNA sequences aimed at silencing the cancer survival protein GRP78 in HER2-positive SKBR3 breast cancer cells. The modified aptamer bound to and entered the cells, but the siRNA gene silencing only worked when a Lipofectamine transfection agent was used, so the delivery formulation matters for these genetic therapies. The work was done in a cell line.

items.title: Identifying patterns of selection at synonymous sites in a Pseudomonas phylogeny
items.summary: The author used a statistical method on sequence comparisons from Pseudomonas bacteria to find DNA changes that do not alter the protein but still appear to be under selection. About 8% of the tested sites in one gene and 7.5% in another were highly constrained, including some already shown by experiments to be beneficial, which suggests these changes may often contribute to adaptation.

items.title: Drivers of insect decline: direct, indirect, and combined pressures
items.venue: Annals of the Entomological Society of America
items.summary: This review sorts the known causes of insect decline using the IPBES assessment framework and attaches confidence statements so policy groups can use the findings directly. Land-use and climate change are well established as drivers, while insecticides, light pollution and the combined effects of multiple stressors are less well understood, though the authors say enough is known to start planning action.

items.title: Pendant Phosphonium Outperforms Ammonium by Strengthening Local Electric Fields in a Ruthenium Hydrogenation Catalyst
items.summary: The researcher compared two versions of a ruthenium catalyst for turning CO2 into methanol, one with a pendant phosphonium group and one with an ammonium group. The phosphonium version gave higher turnover and better selectivity for methanol, and calculations indicate it lowers the energy barrier of the rate-limiting step by stabilizing charge more strongly.

items.title: Measuring display clutter in different contexts: evidence from performance and attention in websites and maps
items.summary: Participants searched for targets on websites and maps while the authors compared three computer algorithms that measure display clutter against search time and eye tracking data. Only feature congestion was linked to response time in both websites and maps, and the results offer guidance on which clutter measures and eye tracking metrics to use for each display type.

items.title: The Silent Spill: Measuring Sensitive Data Leaks Across Public URL Repositories
items.summary: The authors built an automated system to find sensitive information exposed in URLs published by security scanning services, paste sites and web archives. Applied to about 6.1 million URLs, it flagged 12,331 potential exposures involving authentication, financial, personal and document-related content, which shows that accidental leaks through these services are still happening.

items.title: Semantic Factorization for 3D Shape Generation
items.summary: No abstract was available for this paper. Based on the title alone, it concerns semantic factorization for generating 3D shapes.

items.title: Signal-Adapted Kernels and Lazy-Evaluation Gaussian Process Regression
items.summary: The authors developed a kernel for Gaussian process regression that adapts its shape to the data, along with a lazy-evaluation version of the method designed to scale to larger datasets and to keep predictions continuous. They compared the approach with standard methods on rainfall and elevation data, looking at unwanted oscillations and how well the fits follow the contours of the data.

items.title: Pediatric social robotics in ASD: navigating AI blind-spots toward clinical validation
items.summary: This mini-review looks at three areas of social robots for children with autism that have little validation so far: robots paired with wearable sensors, virtual reality and robot hybrids, and generative AI conversation. The authors conclude these systems cannot yet be supported as primary therapy, and they propose a five-module clinical validation roadmap including standardized outcome measures and multisite randomized trials.

items.title: Search for compressed electroweak SUSY production in final states with two $\tau$-leptons in $\sqrt{s} = 13$ and $13.6$ TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
items.venue: CERN Document Server (European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary: This ATLAS collaboration paper searches proton-proton collision data from the Large Hadron Collider for supersymmetric particles (tau-sleptons, charginos and neutralinos) in cases where the particle masses are close together. The results are generally consistent with the Standard Model, with a few deviations of 2.1 to 2.4 sigma, and the paper sets mass limits for some scenarios but none for direct tau-slepton production when all channels are combined.

items.title: Carrier dynamics in neutron irradiated high-quality epitaxial GaN
items.summary: The authors used three measurement techniques to study how charge carriers recombine and become trapped in high-quality gallium nitride layers before and after neutron irradiation. Carrier lifetime fell from about 200 ns to about 2 ps across the conditions studied as radiation defects increased, and the data point to trapping centres at about 0.3 eV, likely linked to carbon and carbon-oxygen complexes.

innovation.screened: Screened, nothing to act on yet: Uncovering the importance of lipofection for aptamer-mediated therapeutic oligonucleotide delivery in a HER2+ SKBR3 breast cancer cell line (evidence: Results come from one cell line (SKBR3). The abstract says the gene silencing depended on a Lipofectamine formulation. That is a lab-scale proof of concept) | Pendant Phosphonium Outperforms Ammonium by Strengthening Local Electric Fields in a Ruthenium Hydrogenation Catalyst (Carleton's role: Marczenko is the fifth of nine authors. The first and last authors are at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory; evidence: This is a mechanistic study of a homogeneous ruthenium complex using operando NMR and computation. It reports no scale-up and no validation beyond the lab) | The Silent Spill: Measuring Sensitive Data Leaks Across Public URL Repositories (Carleton's role: Abdou is the second of four authors. The first and last authors are at Concordia University) | Measuring display clutter in different contexts: evidence from performance and attention in websites and maps (evidence: The study compares three existing clutter algorithms against eye-tracking and response-time data from one lab study of participants. It does not present a new working method or prototype) | Semantic Factorization for 3D Shape Generation (market: The abstract is empty, so I cannot name a product category or customer for this result without guessing; evidence: There is no abstract, so no reported performance or validation is available to assess) | Signal-Adapted Kernels and Lazy-Evaluation Gaussian Process Regression (partner: My search found only open-source GP and interpolation repositories. It did not find a specific operating company, Ottawa or otherwise, that sells this kind of regression; evidence: The abstract describes a working method but reports no performance numbers. It states only that the method was compared on rainfall and elevation datasets for oscillation and smoothing behaviour) | Carrier dynamics in neutron irradiated high-quality epitaxial GaN (market: The paper is a materials characterization of carrier lifetimes and trapping in irradiated GaN layers. I could not tie it to a product category that buys this result today; partner: Novigrad (Saskatoon) does radiation testing for aerospace, defence and nuclear teams, but it works on electronics testing. I did not verify a company active in GaN radiation detectors; Carleton's role: Carleton authors are at positions 6 and 7 of 14. The first and last authors are at Vilnius University; evidence: The paper reports lab measurements on epitaxial GaN samples. It shows no device or prototype) No paper passed all four checks this week, so there are no recommendations. Skipped with no plausible commercial angle: the insect decline review (MacMillan, one of 39 authors); the synonymous-site selection analysis in Pseudomonas (Rodrigue, middle author, basic evolutionary biology); and the pediatric social robotics mini-review (D'Angiulli, a review that states these systems are not yet validated).
